title: US payrolls fall 23,000 in July, denting Fed hike bets; stocks hit records
content: US non-farm payrolls fell by 23,000 in July, data released 7 August showed, confounding forecasts for a roughly 83,000-95,000 gain and reversing June's revised 20,000 rise; May and June were revised down by a combined 103,000. Unemployment eased to 4.1% from 4.2%, mostly reflecting a lower participation rate, while average hourly earnings growth slowed to 3.2% y/y, the weakest since May 2021. Markets read the report as reducing pressure on the Fed to tighten further: the S&P 500 rose 0.6% and the Nasdaq 1.3% to fresh records, the 10-year UST yield eased to around 4.64% from 4.67%, the dollar weakened and gold rallied as traders cut the odds of a September hike to about 44% from 58%.

title: Oil whipsaws as Iran-Oman Hormuz deal talks falter; Brent holds near $83
content: Oil prices whipsawed this week on on-off hopes for a US-brokered deal easing shipping restrictions through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent fell over 6% to below $79/bbl around 3-5 August as Iran and Oman appeared close to an agreement, before rebounding after Tehran published a draft plan on 6 August imposing restrictive conditions, including bans on US and Israeli vessels and penalties on other transiting ships. Brent settled around $83.50/bbl and WTI near $78/bbl by 7 August, leaving crude little changed on the week overall. US officials said a deal could still be reached, but the volatility highlighted lingering geopolitical risk to Gulf energy supply and the inflation outlook.

title: Wall Street hits fresh records as Dow tops 54,000 on strong Q2 earnings
content: US equities rallied to record highs this week, extending gains from a strong Q2 earnings season. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed above 54,000 for the first time on 3 August, up around 1.7% on the day, while the S&P 500 gained a similar amount to close near 7,737 and the Nasdaq Composite rose over 2.5%. Semiconductor and AI-linked stocks led the advance after hyperscalers' results eased concerns over data-centre capital spending, with roughly 80% of Nasdaq volume and 70% of NYSE volume in advancing shares. The rally broadened further on 7 August after the weaker-than-expected jobs report reinforced hopes the Fed will hold off on further tightening.
